## Second trigger: decode back-pressure, 8 slots, 128k shape (the whole pair deadlocks)

The single-slot case above is the simplest reproduction, but the same zero-budget loop is reached with the default `--max-running-requests 8` whenever the decode cannot pull a finished prefill promptly. Observed 2026-10-09 00:00 UTC with the decode's KV pool set to 262,144 tokens(prefill unchanged: 8 slots, 786k pool, radix off) and four 131,072-token prompts at concurrency 4:

| Step | Prefill (SWA pool 19,456 tokens) | Decode (pool 262,144) |
|---|---|---|
| #1 | chunks 8,192 / 2,752 alternating, SWA usage 0.57 / 0.85; transferred | runs #1: 132,096 tokens used; #2 cannot be pre-allocated (130,048 free) |
| #2 | prefilled normally, then **inflight**, waiting for the decode | still running #1 |
| #3 | chunks 2,112 → 8,192 → **640**, SWA usage **0.96 → 0.99**; then no batch ever again | #1 finishes at 00:00:20; pre-allocates #2 and starts the pull |
| after | loop spins in `get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run` → `process_prefill_chunk` → `cache_unfinished_disagg_prefill` (py-spy) | loop spins in `pop_transferred` → `maybe_start_pull` / `_start_chunked_pull`; KV never arrives |

An 8-token request sent afterwards got no answer in 55 s; both `/health` endpoints return 200; no watchdog fires. Of the four client
requests one completed and three timed out after 1,200 s; the queues drained only when those clients disconnected.

**Why 8 slots is not enough.** The pool is sized as two chunks plus a 384-token hold (`window + interval + 2 pages`) per slot. That hold is right for a request that is *between chunks*: its previous chunk's SWA pages were evicted when the next chunk ran. A request whose prefill has **finished** but whose KV the decode has not pulled has no next chunk, so nothing evicts its last chunk's SWA pages: the hold is ~8k tokens, not 384. One such inflight request plus the chunk in flight for the next request fills 19,456 tokens, the continuation budget `remaining_swa − (window + page)` is 0, no batch forms, and `maybe_evict_swa` never runs. The decode cannot pull until the prefill loop progresses, and the prefill cannot progress until the decode pulls, so the pair is wedged. Any decode back-pressure (a full decode pool, a slow decode, a held handshake such as our F-12) opens this window; a small decode pool only makes it easy to hit on demand.
